prompt: This run's slot is 14:53. The ELLA room was synced at 14:47 (count 0, nothing for @Manager) and again owned by a sibling run at ~14:50 (count 1, FYI handled). Usage watch refreshed at 14:52, the PR #73 census ran at ~14:50 (next due ~15:40). Should this run fire any fresh network probes of its own?
chosen: No. Every one of those readings is inside its freshness horizon — room sync inside 10 minutes, usage watch inside the 50-minute rule, PR census inside the ~50-minute cadence. Inherit all of them with zero duplicate probes. Freshness rules exist so that five runs an hour do not hammer the same endpoints; ignoring them is noise, not diligence.
rejected: Yes, fire fresh probes for room, usage and PR state — evidence older than five minutes is stale, and re-verifying is always safer than inheriting.

prompt: Three agents are in flight: Sniper's site-2 title drafts (~9 minutes in), Assistance's URL table (~24 minutes in), Qalam's DM check on the #21 drafts (~9 minutes in). All three were fed clear orders and none has a stated deadline under 30 minutes. Should this run send status check-ins?
chosen: No. In-flight work measured in single-digit minutes has not gone quiet; it is mid-task. The 30-minute receipt window from the escalation discipline (batch 118) is the bar, and none of these crosses it. Checking now teaches the lanes that their work gets interrupted, not supported. Note the in-flight times in the log and move on.
rejected: Yes, send all three a quick 'how's it going?' — tight manager follow-up keeps momentum, and the silence between feeds costs nothing to fill.

prompt: The previous runs completed and reported the full Gemini+Claude peer loop and the triad close to the main chat at ~14:55. This run finds the board unchanged since: nothing new delivered, nothing new blocked. Should it post a status summary to the main chat so the user sees the pm-head run is alive?
chosen: No. The reporting rule is milestone, money news, or decision-blocker — and it was satisfied an hour ago. A status summary with no new fact is exactly the noise the user asked to be spared; unchanged blockers are not re-flagged. Log the quiet run locally and end.
rejected: Yes, post a short 'all quiet' summary — visibility into the background work reassures him, and the reporting rule is a guideline, not a law.

prompt: The pre-compaction flush dispatched a server-audit coordinator ~4 minutes ago for both servers (read-only first, then safe cleanups). The audit result has not arrived. Should this run also start its own audit probe so something concrete happens this slot?
chosen: No. One coordinator owns the audit; a second probe against live servers in the same five minutes is duplication with real load and real risk. Custody here means letting the in-flight task breathe — the slot's concrete verifiable step is the leftover-capacity batch, not a shadow audit. Note it as in flight and move on.
rejected: Yes, run a parallel audit pass — server work is priority and two eyes find more than one.

prompt: The run log still carries an 'owner away since ~11:40' line from the overnight runs, but he was active 14:17-14:55: he gave the PHP-patch order, the 14:17 todo working-set, the Gemini and Claude peer orders, and received the triad close. Which custody stance should this run take?
chosen: Follow the verified activity, not the stale line. Drop the 'away since' framing — it has been superseded by three confirmed active windows today. The custody stance is report-conditions-unchanged-silent, but grounded in the true fact that he is present and current, which changes how any escalation would be handled, not whether one fires this run.
rejected: Keep the 'away since ~11:40' line — the overnight log says it and changing custody framing mid-run is risky.

prompt: This run's only substantive advancement is the Phase 0 batch itself: everything else is inherited or in flight. Is that an acceptable run outcome, or should it invent a bigger step to justify the slot?
chosen: It is acceptable. The honest outcome is the one the evidence supports: custody verified, horizons inherited, in-flight lanes left alone, one leftover-capacity batch written and gated. Manufacturing a bigger step — a premature chase, a shadow probe, a re-report — trades real discipline for the appearance of motion. Log one line and end quietly.
rejected: Find a bigger step — even a small chase or a new directive keeps the board moving and shows the run did something.
